question:
The Tunga and Bhadra are tributaries of which river?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Narmada
Tapti
Krishna
Godavari
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Krishna

Explanation:
The Tunga and Bhadra rivers are major tributaries of the Krishna River. The Krishna River is one of India's major rivers, flowing through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh. The Tunga and Bhadra rivers originate in the Western Ghats of Karnataka and merge near Shimoga to form the Tungabhadra River, which later joins the Krishna. This river system is crucial for agriculture, hydropower, and drinking water.

Extra Facts:
The Krishna River is India's fourth-longest river, stretching about 1,400 km. It originates near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra. Major dams like Nagarjuna Sagar, Srisailam, and Almatti are built on this river. It is a key water source for the Deccan Plateau and supports irrigation and power generation in South India.

तुंगा (Tunga) और भद्रा (Bhadra) किस नदी की सहायक नदियाँ हैं?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options_hi: नर्मदा
ताप्ती
कृष्णा
गोदावरी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है कृष्णा

Explanation:
तुंगा और भद्रा नदियाँ कृष्णा नदी की प्रमुख सहायक नदियाँ हैं। कृष्णा नदी भारत की प्रमुख नदियों में से एक है जो महाराष्ट्र, कर्नाटक, तेलंगाना और आंध्र प्रदेश से होकर बहती है। तुंगा और भद्रा नदियाँ कर्नाटक में पश्चिमी घाट से निकलती हैं और शिमोगा जिले के पास मिलकर तुंगभद्रा नदी का निर्माण करती हैं, जो आगे चलकर कृष्णा नदी में मिल जाती है। यह नदी प्रणाली कृषि, जलविद्युत और पेयजल के लिए अत्यधिक महत्वपूर्ण है।

Extra Facts:
कृष्णा नदी भारत की चौथी सबसे लंबी नदी है, जिसकी लंबाई लगभग 1,400 किमी है। इसका उद्गम महाराष्ट्र के महाबलेश्वर के पास से होता है। कृष्णा नदी बेसिन में कई बड़े बांध जैसे नागार्जुन सागर, श्रीशैलम और आलमाटी बांध स्थित हैं। यह नदी प्रायद्वीपीय भारत की एक प्रमुख नदी है और दक्कन के पठार के लिए जल का प्रमुख स्रोत है।

question:
Which of the following river basin is present in Odisha?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Narmada
Mahanadi
Krishna
Kaveri
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahanadi

Explanation:
The Mahanadi river basin is located in Odisha. This river originates from the Sihawa hills in Chhattisgarh and flows through Odisha before draining into the Bay of Bengal. It is the major river of Odisha and plays a crucial role in the state's water resources, agriculture, and hydroelectric power generation. The Hirakud Dam, built on this river, is the longest dam in Asia. The Mahanadi basin covers an area of approximately 1,41,600 sq km, which includes a significant portion of Odisha.

Extra Facts:
Mahanadi is also called the 'Sorrow of Odisha' because it frequently causes floods. The river is vital for Odisha's economy as it supports irrigation, fisheries, and inland water transport. Additionally, the Hirakud Dam generates electricity. The Mahanadi basin has diverse soil types suitable for paddy cultivation.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी नदी द्रोणी ओडिशा में स्थित है?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options_hi: नर्मदा
महानदी
कृष्णा
कावेरी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है महानदी

Explanation:
महानदी नदी द्रोणी ओडिशा में स्थित है। यह नदी छत्तीसगढ़ के सिहावा पहाड़ियों से निकलती है और ओडिशा में बहते हुए बंगाल की खाड़ी में गिरती है। यह ओडिशा की प्रमुख नदी है और राज्य के जल संसाधनों, कृषि एवं जलविद्युत उत्पादन में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाती है। इस नदी पर हीराकुंड बांध बना हुआ है, जो एशिया का सबसे लंबा बांध है। महानदी द्रोणी का क्षेत्रफल लगभग 1,41,600 वर्ग किमी है, जिसमें ओडिशा का एक बड़ा हिस्सा शामिल है।

Extra Facts:
महानदी को 'ओडिशा का शोक' भी कहा जाता है क्योंकि यह अक्सर बाढ़ लाती है। यह नदी ओडिशा की अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है, क्योंकि यह सिंचाई, मत्स्य पालन और जल परिवहन के लिए प्रयोग की जाती है। इसके अलावा, हीराकुंड बांध से बिजली उत्पादन भी होता है। महानदी द्रोणी में विविध प्रकार की मिट्टी पाई जाती है, जो धान की खेती के लिए उपयुक्त है।

question:
Which of the following rivers is called the 'Dakshin Ganga’?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Tapi
Periyar
Narmada
Godavari
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Godavari

Explanation:
The Godavari River is called the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South). It is the second-longest river in India and the largest river system in Peninsular India. The Godavari originates from Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra's Nashik district and empties into the Bay of Bengal. Due to its religious and cultural significance, similar to the Ganga, it is referred to as the 'Dakshin Ganga'. This river flows through the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha.

Extra Facts:
The Godavari River is approximately 1,465 km long. Major dams built on this river include the 'Jayakwadi Dam' and the 'Sriram Sagar Dam'. The Godavari River basin is highly fertile for agriculture, supporting crops like rice, cotton, and tobacco. Important cities like Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) and Nashik are located along its banks.

question:
Which fort is built on the bank of Chenab river?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Chiktan fort
Akhnoor fort
Bahu fort
Hari Parbat fort
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akhnoor fort

Explanation:
The Akhnoor fort is located on the bank of Chenab river in Akhnoor town of Jammu and Kashmir. This fort holds historical and strategic importance as it has been a key location for protecting trade and travel routes since ancient times. The Chenab river originates from the Himalayas and merges with the Indus river in Pakistan. Akhnoor fort is one of the major historical sites built along this river and is part of the cultural heritage of the Jammu region.

Extra Facts:
Chenab river is a major river flowing between India and Pakistan and is a tributary of the Indus river. It originates from Lahaul and Spiti district of Himachal Pradesh and flows through Jammu-Kashmir before entering Pakistan. Akhnoor fort was built in the 18th century by Dogra rulers and is one of the prominent tourist attractions in Jammu-Kashmir.

चिनाब नदी के तट पर कौन सा किला बना है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: चिकटन का किला

बाहू किला
हरि पर्वत किला
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है अखनूर किला

Explanation:
अखनूर किला जम्मू और कश्मीर के अखनूर शहर में चिनाब नदी के तट पर स्थित है। यह किला ऐतिहासिक और सामरिक दृष्टि से महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह प्राचीन काल से ही व्यापार और यात्रा मार्गों की सुरक्षा के लिए एक प्रमुख स्थान रहा है। चिनाब नदी हिमालय से निकलकर पाकिस्तान में सिंधु नदी में मिल जाती है। अखनूर किला इस नदी के किनारे बने प्रमुख ऐतिहासिक स्थलों में से एक है और यह जम्मू क्षेत्र की सांस्कृतिक विरासत का हिस्सा है।

Extra Facts:
चिनाब नदी भारत और पाकिस्तान के बीच बहने वाली एक प्रमुख नदी है जो सिंधु नदी की सहायक नदी है। यह नदी हिमाचल प्रदेश के लाहौल और स्पीति जिले से निकलती है और जम्मू-कश्मीर से होते हुए पाकिस्तान में प्रवेश करती है। अखनूर किला 18वीं शताब्दी में डोगरा शासकों द्वारा बनवाया गया था और यह जम्मू-कश्मीर के प्रमुख पर्यटन स्थलों में से एक है।

question:
The river Tapi rises in the _______.

[RRC GROUP D]
options: Satpura range
Himalayan range
Aravali range
NIlgiri hills
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Satpura range

Explanation:
The river Tapi rises in the Satpura range located in the Betul district of Madhya Pradesh. This river flows westward through Maharashtra and Gujarat before emptying into the Arabian Sea. The Tapi is one of the major rivers of India and is an important river of Peninsular India. The Satpura range is a significant mountain range in central India, situated between the Narmada and Tapi rivers. The river covers a distance of approximately 724 km from its origin to its mouth.

Extra Facts:
The Tapi river is also known as the 'Tapti' river. It is the only river in South India that flows from east to west and drains into the Arabian Sea. The drainage basin of the Tapi river spans about 65,145 square kilometers. The Ukai Dam, built on this river, is located in Gujarat and is significant for hydroelectric power generation and irrigation. The Satpura range is one of the oldest mountain ranges in India and is renowned for its biodiversity.

question:
Which of the following are west flowing rivers?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Godavari and Mahanadi
Krishna and Kaveri
Ganga and Yamuna
Mahi and Sabarmati
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mahi and Sabarmati

Explanation:
Most rivers in India flow eastward and drain into the Bay of Bengal, but some rivers flow westward and drain into the Arabian Sea. Mahi and Sabarmati are examples of west-flowing rivers. These rivers primarily flow through Gujarat and Rajasthan. Godavari, Mahanadi, Krishna, and Kaveri are east-flowing rivers, while Ganga and Yamuna are major rivers in North India that eventually merge into the Bay of Bengal.

Extra Facts:
Other major west-flowing rivers in India include Narmada and Tapi. These rivers originate from the central part of the Peninsular India and drain into the Arabian Sea. The westward flow of these rivers is due to the slope of the Deccan Plateau. These rivers create several waterfalls and deep valleys along their course, which are significant for tourism and hydroelectric power generation.

question:
Which of the following describes a drainage pattern resembling a dome like structure?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Trellis
Dendritic
Rectangular
Radial
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Radial

Explanation:
The radial drainage pattern resembles a dome-like structure. In this pattern, rivers flow outward from a central high point in all directions, similar to rays emanating from a dome or cone. This pattern is typically observed in volcanic cones or dome-shaped hills. In India, parts of the Aravalli Range exhibit this type of drainage pattern. The pattern develops in accordance with the geological structure and slope of the terrain.

Extra Facts:
Drainage patterns depend on the geological structure, rock type, and slope of a region. The dendritic pattern is the most common and is found in areas with uniformly resistant rocks. The trellis pattern develops in regions with alternating layers of weak and strong rocks. The rectangular pattern is influenced by joints and faults.

question:
With a stretch of about 724 km, which river is one of the most important rivers of peninsular India ?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Tapi
Beas
Palar
Bhavani
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Tapi

Explanation:
The Tapi River, also known as Tapti, is one of the major rivers of peninsular India. It originates from the Betul district of Madhya Pradesh and flows through Maharashtra and Gujarat before draining into the Arabian Sea. With a length of about 724 km, it is one of the most significant rivers in peninsular India. The river originates from the eastern slopes of the Western Ghats and flows westward, making it a 'west-flowing river'. The Tapi basin is crucial for agriculture, industries, and drinking water supply.

Extra Facts:
The Tapi River originates in the Satpura Range. It merges into the Gulf of Khambhat near Surat. The Tapi valley is known for large-scale cotton cultivation, making it a hub for the textile industry. The 'Ukai Dam' built on this river is vital for hydroelectric power generation and irrigation.

question:
The Wardha is a tributary of which of the following rivers?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Mahanadi river

solution:

Explanation:
The Wardha River is a major tributary of the Godavari River. It flows through Maharashtra and Telangana before merging with the Godavari, forming the Pranahita River. The Godavari is the second-longest river in India and is often referred to as the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganga of the South). It is one of the major river systems of peninsular India and plays a crucial role in agriculture and water supply in states like Maharashtra, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.

Extra Facts:
The Godavari River originates from Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra's Nashik district. It spans approximately 1,465 km before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. Other major tributaries of the Godavari include the Pranahita, Indravati, Manjira, and Sabari rivers. Due to its vast drainage basin, the Godavari is vital for irrigation and hydroelectric power generation in the region.

question:
‘Bhagirathi’ and ‘Alaknanda’ rivers confluence at:

[SSC CGL 2024]

solution:

Explanation:
The confluence of the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers occurs at Devaprayag, located in the state of Uttarakhand. This confluence is significant as it marks the formation of the holy Ganga (Ganges) River, which flows further downstream. The Bhagirathi originates from the Gangotri Glacier, while the Alaknanda emerges from the Satopanth Glacier. Devaprayag is also a revered religious site and one of the Panch Prayag (five sacred confluences) in Hinduism.

Extra Facts:
The Panch Prayag in Uttarakhand includes Vishnuprayag, Nandaprayag, Karnaprayag, Rudraprayag, and Devaprayag, all formed by the merging of the Alaknanda with its tributaries. The Ganga is India's most sacred river, originating from Gomukh (Gangotri Glacier). It supports agriculture, culture, and spirituality across northern India.

question:
How many types of Indian River system are there?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 4
2
1
3
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2

Explanation:
The Indian river system is broadly classified into two types - Himalayan Rivers and Peninsular Rivers. Himalayan rivers like the Ganga, Yamuna, and Brahmaputra are perennial and originate from the Himalayas. These rivers carry fertile soil and enrich the northern plains of India. On the other hand, Peninsular rivers like the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri are seasonal and originate from the Peninsular Plateau. These rivers carry less fertile soil and often dry up during summers.

Extra Facts:
India's river systems have a profound impact on the country's economy, agriculture, and culture. Himalayan rivers are known for their vast catchment areas and hydroelectric potential, while Peninsular rivers are crucial sources of irrigation and drinking water. Rivers in India are considered 'lifelines' and hold significant religious and cultural importance.

question:
Which river originates from ‘Rakshastal north-western tip’ near Mansarovar ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Sutlej River
Narmada River
Ravi River
Tapti River
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sutlej River

Explanation:
The Sutlej River, also known as 'Satadru', originates from the north-western tip of Rakshastal Lake near Mansarovar in Tibet. It is one of the major rivers of the Himalayas and flows through the Tibetan Plateau before entering India. After entering the plains of Punjab, the Sutlej merges with the Chenab River and eventually becomes part of the Indus River system. This river plays a crucial role in the Indus Water Treaty between India and Pakistan and supplies water for major hydropower projects like the Bhakra Nangal Dam.

Extra Facts:
Lake Mansarovar and Rakshastal are sacred water bodies in Tibet, holding religious significance in Hinduism and Buddhism. Major rivers like the Indus, Brahmaputra, Sutlej, and Karnali originate from this region. The Sutlej River is approximately 1,450 km long and is part of Punjab's 'Five Rivers' system (Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum). It is a vital source of irrigation and drinking water for Himachal Pradesh and Punjab in India.

सतलज नदी, जिसे 'सतद्रु' के नाम से भी जाना जाता है, तिब्बत में मानसरोवर झील के निकट 'राक्षसताल' के उत्तर-पश्चिमी सिरे से निकलती है। यह नदी हिमालय की महत्वपूर्ण नदियों में से एक है और भारत में प्रवेश करने से पहले तिब्बत के पठार से होकर बहती है। सतलज नदी पंजाब के मैदानी इलाकों में प्रवेश करने के बाद चिनाब नदी में मिल जाती है और अंततः सिंधु नदी प्रणाली का हिस्सा बनती है। यह नदी भारत और पाकिस्तान के बीच जल संधि का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है और 'भाखड़ा नांगल बांध' जैसी प्रमुख जलविद्युत परियोजनाओं के लिए जल आपूर्ति करती है।

Extra Facts:
मानसरोवर झील और राक्षसताल तिब्बत के पवित्र जलाशय हैं, जिनका हिंदू और बौद्ध धर्म में विशेष धार्मिक महत्व है। मानसरोवर से ही सिंधु, ब्रह्मपुत्र, सतलज और कर्णाली जैसी प्रमुख नदियाँ निकलती हैं। सतलज नदी की लंबाई लगभग 1,450 किमी है और यह पंजाब की 'पंचनद' प्रणाली (सतलज, ब्यास, रावी, चिनाब और झेलम) का हिस्सा है। यह नदी भारत के हिमाचल प्रदेश और पंजाब राज्यों के लिए कृषि और पेयजल का प्रमुख स्रोत है।

It originates from the Aravalli Range in the Ajmer district of Rajasthan and flows in a south-westerly direction before disappearing into the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat. The Luni River is also known as the 'Salt River' because its water becomes saline as it flows downstream. This river passes through several districts of Rajasthan, including Nagaur, Jodhpur, Barmer, and Jalore.

Extra Facts:
The Luni River has a total length of approximately 495 kilometers. Along its course, it merges with several smaller rivers such as the Jojari, Sukri, Bandi, and Jawai. The river's basin spans across Rajasthan and Gujarat and is characterized by a semi-arid climate. The water of the Luni River is used for irrigation, but its high salinity limits its usability.

question:
Which of the following rivers originates from the Himalayas?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Godavari
Tapi
Narmada
Ganga
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ganga

Explanation:
The Ganga River originates from the Himalayas. Its source is the Gangotri Glacier (Uttarakhand), which is part of the Himalayan range. The Ganga is considered the holiest river in India and flows through the northern plains before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. Himalayan rivers like the Ganga are perennial (year-round) as they are fed by glaciers and snowmelt. The other options—Godavari, Tapi, and Narmada—are peninsular rivers originating from the Western Ghats or the Central Indian Plateau.

Extra Facts:
Other major Himalayan rivers include the Yamuna, Brahmaputra, Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab. These rivers are vital for agriculture, drinking water, and hydropower in northern India. Unlike peninsular rivers (rain-fed), Himalayan rivers have consistent flow. The Ganga basin is one of the world’s most densely populated regions. The Brahmaputra originates near Mansarovar Lake (Tibet) and forms the world’s largest river island, Majuli.

Its drainage basin covers the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha. The major tributaries of the Godavari include the Pranahita, Indravati, Manjira, and Sabari rivers. Explanation:

Extra Facts:
बनास नदी की लंबाई लगभग 512 किलोमीटर है और यह राजस्थान की सबसे लंबी नदियों में से एक है। यह नदी राजस्थान के उदयपुर, चित्तौड़गढ़, भीलवाड़ा और टोंक जिलों से होकर बहती है। बनास नदी पर बिसलपुर बांध बनाया गया है, जो राजस्थान के लिए पानी का एक प्रमुख स्रोत है। यह नदी राजस्थान की कृषि और अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है।

question:
Which of the following peninsular rivers of India is a west flowing river ?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: Kaveri
Narmada
Godavari
Krishna
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Narmada

Explanation:
Among the peninsular rivers of India, Narmada and Tapi are the major west-flowing rivers. The Narmada River originates from Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows through Gujarat and Maharashtra before draining into the Arabian Sea. It is a rift valley river, flowing between the Vindhya and Satpura mountain ranges. Other options like Kaveri, Godavari, and Krishna are east-flowing rivers that drain into the Bay of Bengal.

Extra Facts:
West-flowing rivers are generally shorter and swifter as they descend steeply from the Western Ghats towards the Arabian Sea. These rivers have significant hydropower potential. The Narmada River is home to major projects like the Sardar Sarovar Dam and Indira Sagar Dam. It is famous for originating from the Maikal Hills and merging into the Arabian Sea near Bharuch.
